claims.source: Board inference from Raytheon's documented sensor contracts
claims.text: Raytheon holds the sensor data and calibration records underlying the military UAP imagery Congress has repeatedly failed to obtain. Reasoning: it is the manufacturer of the relevant systems and data rights typically follow the contract, but no specific withheld dataset has been identified in a public record.
claims.unresolved: the board's own inference; it names no source that resolves

connections.edgeLabel: sensor-side prime - the contractor-generated data category nobody is asking for
connections.label: Federal Contracting Mechanics
connections.note: Raytheon builds the AN/APG-79 and ATFLIR families through which the military detects and images the objects at issue, which makes it the corporate custodian of a withheld category of contractor-generated sensor data distinct from the custody allegation. Graded Tier 2: no source places Raytheon in any UAP-specific contract vehicle, and the edge rests on documented prime-contractor role plus hearing-record discussion of sensor data.

connections.edgeLabel: Raytheon-built ATFLIR pod produced the FLIR1 record
connections.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
connections.note: The Advanced Targeting Forward Looking Infrared pod is built by Raytheon and is, in the Navy's own words, 'the primary weapons delivery targeting sensor for the U.S. Navy' on F/A-18 C, E and F variants. The Department released three genuine Navy videos in April 2020, one of them from November 2004. Tier 2 because neither document states which sensor produced that video: the contractor's own page on the subject returns 404 and navair.navy.mil returns 403, so the specific tie between the pod and the FLIR1 footage is inference from the aircraft type and the period, not a documented statement.

desc: Raytheon's place in this domain is sensor-side rather than custody-side, and the distinction matters for how the board grades it. It builds the radar and electro-optical systems - the AN/APG-79 and ATFLIR families among them - through which the US military actually detects and images the objects at issue, which makes it the corporate custodian of a different and equally withheld category of material: raw sensor data and the calibration records needed to evaluate it. USAspending records more than a hundred billion dollars in prime contract obligations to Raytheon entities since FY2008, including test-assessment and anomaly-resolution task orders on fighter sensor systems. No sworn witness has named Raytheon as a holder of recovered material. It is included here as a named prime in the 'metal benders' category David Grusch described - contractors 'actually doing specific performance on government contracts' - and because the sensor-data custody question is the one place where the contractor holdings that matter are unambiguously real, unambiguously government-funded, and unambiguously not in congressional hands.
label: Raytheon (RTX Corporation)
